_note: Generated from DCAT-AP-UK. Names match the metadata weaver, so records written by the weaver load into these definitions. Not tested against a live tenant. Create each with CreateCustomProperty in a namespace, then set values as custom property members on entities.

customProperties.description: The name of the resource, in plain English.
A plain English account of what the resource contains and what it can be used for.
The main identifier of the resource in the publisher's own catalogue.
The organisation responsible for making the resource available.
Where to ask questions about the resource or give feedback on it.
Who can get the data, and on what terms.
The classification under the Government Security Classifications Policy that the data itself carries.
The licence under which the resource can be used.
How often the resource is updated.
Whether the resource is a critical data asset under the Data Asset Management Policy.
The organisation that created or compiled the content of the resource.
The date the content of the resource was created or compiled.
A standard, specification or schema the resource follows.
The period of time the data is about.
Whether the data contains information about identifiable living people, and in what form.
A statement of any restriction on access or use, such as the data sharing agreement or legal gateway needed.
The date the content of the resource last changed.
The date the resource was first made available.
A one-sentence summary of the resource, of no more than 250 characters.
The broad subject of the resource, from a controlled list.
Words or short phrases that people might search for, not already in the title or description.
The geographic area the data is about.
A form in which the data can be got, such as a file or an API.
A web page where people can find out about the resource and how to get it.
The version of the resource.
Whether the data contains information that needs extra care beyond being personal, such as special category data.
An organisation and the role it plays for the resource, such as data owner or data steward.
The language or languages of the resource.
Another name the resource is known by, such as an abbreviation or a former name.
Any other identifier the resource is known by, such as one in a national or sector register.
The dataset series this dataset belongs to.
A newer resource that replaces this one.
The date after which the resource should no longer be used.
The version this one replaces in a sequence.
What changed in this version.
The smallest distance the data can tell apart, in metres.
The smallest period the data can tell apart, as an ISO 8601 duration.
A code list, classification or set of groupings the data uses, such as age bands or a geography.
A link to a published statement or measurement of the quality of the data.
Another resource closely related to this one, such as the report the data supports.
A related resource together with the kind of relationship.
A web page that documents the resource, such as a user guide or a methodology.
Who is allowed to see the metadata record itself.
Legislation that requires, governs or permits the publication or sharing of the resource.
A machine-readable policy, in the W3C Open Digital Rights Language (ODRL), saying what may and may not be done with the resource.
Every country or territory where the data is stored or processed, or to which it is sent.
The basis under UK GDPR on which personal data in the resource may be sent outside the UK.
A property this record leaves empty on purpose, and why.
